# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

## Scope: must-have vs stretch

| Phases | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |

must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower

## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)

| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |

| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |

timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.

Consequences:

- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.

  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.

## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)

Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.

One crate, `gba_emu`, with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`. The `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native
debug binary run on the host without wasm.

  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation
  cpu/arm.rs      ARM (32-bit) decode + execute
  cpu/thumb.rs    THUMB (16-bit) decode + execute
  ppu/mod.rs      line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, line compositor, framebuffer
  ppu/bg_text.rs  tiled backgrounds (modes 0-2)
  ppu/bg_affine.rs rotation/scaling backgrounds
  ppu/bitmap.rs   modes 3/4/5
  ppu/obj.rs      sprites (normal + affine)
  ppu/effects.rs  windows, blending, mosaic

  dma.rs          4 DMA channels, triggers, priority

Contracts fixed in Phase 0:

1. **Bus.** `fn read32(&mut self, addr: u32) -> u32` and the other widths, plus a cycle cost for each
   access. The CPU only talks to the bus, never to components directly.
2. **IO registers.** `io.rs` maps address ranges to owners: PPU `0x000-0x05F`, APU `0x060-0x0AF`,
   DMA `0x0B0-0x0DF`, timers `0x100-0x10F`, serial `0x120-0x12F` and `0x134-0x15F` (stub: plain storage, never
   connected), keypad `0x130-0x133`, IRQ/system `0x200-0x804`. Each owner
   exposes `io_read16(offset)` and `io_write16(offset, value)`, with 8- and 32-bit accesses split or
   merged centrally in `io.rs`. Each owner starts as a stub that its agent later fills in.
3. **Interrupts.** Any component calls `irq.request(IrqSource::VBlank)` etc. Only the CPU consumes interrupts.
4. **Timing.** `cpu.step()` returns the cycles it used. `Gba::run_frame()` loops until 280,896 cycles
   (228 lines x 1232 cycles) have elapsed, advancing PPU, timers, DMA and APU by the same cycles.
   Where exactly a frame ends (start of VBlank or not) must match Mesen2. Verify this in Phase 0 by
   comparing early frames with the reference.
5. **Events between components.** The PPU signals HBlank/VBlank to DMA. Timers signal FIFO ticks to the
   APU, and the APU signals FIFO-empty to DMA. These go through plain method calls in `gba.rs`, not
   through components holding references to each other.
6. **BIOS.** `gba-eval/spec/gba_bios_stub.bin` is embedded with `include_bytes!` and mapped at
   `0x00000000`. The CPU starts at the reset vector in ARM mode and runs it as normal code.
7. **ABI.** All 10 exports exist from day one. No imports: no `std::println!` in the wasm build,
   no threads, no allocation after init on hot paths. Do not export `emu_boot_frames`.

## 4. Workflow: agents, review, tracking

**Parallel agents.**
- Agent definitions live in `.claude/agents/`, one per role below plus `reviewer`. Prompts per phase
  are in `EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md`.
- Give each agent its own git worktree and branch (`phase1/arm`, `phase1/thumb`, ...).
- An agent only edits the files it owns in the phase table. Shared files belong to the integrator
  (you, or one coordinating agent).
- Brief each agent with three things: its phase row, `CLAUDE.md`, and its gbatek sections.
- Keep it to 4 agents at most per phase. More than that and integration costs more than it saves.

**Fast feedback loop (minutes, not 10).**
- Unit tests (`cargo test`, native, seconds) for decoder and ALU edge cases.
- `cargo run --bin run_rom -- <rom> <frames> out.ppm` for any ROM, including the ungraded dev ROMs
  under `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/test/`. Many of them print PASS/FAIL or a failing test number on screen.
- `scripts/grade-subset.sh <wasm> <run-name> <testcase ids...>` grades only the named testcases with
  the real grader (2 short tests took about 7 s). Read the per-testcase lines it prints. The section
  totals are meaningless for a subset.

**Milestone loop (about 10 min).** Run `scripts/grade-full.sh phase-<n> "note"` at the end of each phase,
after committing. It builds the wasm, runs the full grader, appends a row to `scores.tsv`
(date, phase, commit, overall, replay, procedural, audio, note), and saves `summary.json` plus the score row
under `results/milestones/phase-<n>/`. Commit both. All other `results/` output is git-ignored.

**Merge checklist (integrator).**
1. The branch only touches the files it owns.
2. `cargo test` and the wasm build pass.
3. The smoke set does not regress. The phase gate tests improve.
4. A review agent, which did not write the code, reads the diff against the gbatek sections. It checks
   for mistakes and for anything that looks like it came from another emulator (unusual names, comments
   or structure that the spec doesn't explain). Use a fresh context with no access to the author's chat.
5. Merge to `main`, then rerun the smoke set on `main`.

**Tracking.**
- `scores.tsv` holds one row per milestone, and `results/milestones/` holds each milestone's `summary.json`.
- `NOTES.md` logs decisions (date, what, why) and the agents and models used per phase.
- `TIMELOG.md` is the human's own hours log.
- Keep the `results/` folders of the last good run per phase, so you can diff `.cand.png` files when
  something regresses.

---

## 5. Risks and likely problems

1. **CPU bugs look like graphics bugs.** A wrong flag in one instruction can show up as a broken sprite
   three phases later. Finish Phase 1 properly, using the ungraded jsmolka ROMs, before moving on.
2. **Replay drift.** Small timing errors shift the moment input lands, and the game diverges. This is
   the biggest score risk and the hardest to debug. Mitigate by checking frame alignment in Phase 0 and
   doing cycle timing in Phase 5.
3. **Frame boundary mismatch.** If `emu_run_frame` stops at a different point in the frame than Mesen2,
   every frame is offset. Check this against the reference early.
4. **Audio rate mismatch.** See Phase 4. Easy to get silently wrong.
5. **Games hanging on save hardware.** Many games wait forever for a Flash or EEPROM reply. A black
   screen on a replay usually means this.
6. **Shared-file conflicts** between parallel agents. Prevented by the ownership table. Expect
   contract changes anyway and route them through the integrator.
7. **Originality.**
   - Models have seen open-source emulators in training and may reproduce their structure.
   - The review step checks for this, and `.claude/settings.json` blocks reads of
     `gba-eval/candidates`, `gba-eval/third_party`, `mesen_step.cpp` and web access.
   - The block only applies to Claude Code agents launched from this repo. Other agent tools need
     the same rule in their own config.
   - Shell commands that don't name those folders directly can still reach them. Treat the block as a
     guard rail, not proof.
8. **Overfitting.** An agent may "fix" a test by special-casing it. `CLAUDE.md` forbids branching on ROM
   identity, and the review step checks for it.
9. **Endstate tests are all-or-nothing.** One wrong pixel scores ~0. A test that "looks right" can
   still score 0. Compare `.cand.png` with `.ref.png` pixel by pixel.
10. **Fuel limit.** A slow PPU (per-pixel work with lots of branching) can trap on heavy games.
    Measure in Phase 6, or earlier if a replay "skips".
11. **Score ceiling.** The maximum is 0.96, not 1.0 (the `comprehensive` subsystem has no tests). Tell the
    client so expectations are set correctly.
12. **Grader runtime.** A full grade takes about 10 minutes and uses all CPU cores. Running two at once
    slows both. Set `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` if you must.

1. **Bus.** `fn read32(&mut self, addr: u32) -> u32` and the other widths, plus a cycle cost for each
   access. The CPU only talks to the bus, never to components directly.
2. **IO registers.** `io.rs` maps address ranges to owners: PPU `0x000-0x05F`, APU `0x060-0x0AF`,
   DMA `0x0B0-0x0DF`, timers `0x100-0x10F`, serial `0x120-0x12F` and `0x134-0x15F` (stub: plain storage, never
   connected), keypad `0x130-0x133`, IRQ/system `0x200-0x804`. Each owner
   exposes `io_read16(offset)` and `io_write16(offset, value)`, with 8- and 32-bit accesses split or
   merged centrally in `io.rs`. Each owner starts as a stub that its agent later fills in.
3. **Interrupts.** Any component calls `irq.request(IrqSource::VBlank)` etc. Only the CPU consumes interrupts.
4. **Timing.** `cpu.step()` returns the cycles it used. `Gba::run_frame()` loops until 280,896 cycles
   (228 lines x 1232 cycles) have elapsed, advancing PPU, timers, DMA and APU by the same cycles.
   Where exactly a frame ends (start of VBlank or not) must match Mesen2. Verify this in Phase 0 by
   comparing early frames with the reference.
5. **Events between components.** The PPU signals HBlank/VBlank to DMA. Timers signal FIFO ticks to the
   APU, and the APU signals FIFO-empty to DMA. These go through plain method calls in `gba.rs`, not
   through components holding references to each other.
6. **BIOS.** `gba-eval/spec/gba_bios_stub.bin` is embedded with `include_bytes!` and mapped at
   `0x00000000`. The CPU starts at the reset vector in ARM mode and runs it as normal code.
7. **ABI.** All 10 exports exist from day one. No imports: no `std::println!` in the wasm build,
   no threads, no allocation after init on hot paths. Do not export `emu_boot_frames`.

Phase 0 deliverable: the ABI works end to end, the BIOS is mapped, and the CPU can be a stub.
`run_rom` writes a black frame. `scripts/grade-subset.sh ... smoke <any test>` runs without
"skip: trapped" (score ~0 is expected).

---

## 3. Phases

Each phase lists its agents (run in parallel), the files they own, and the test that shows it worked.
"Gate" means the integrator merges the phase only when the gate passes.

Smoke set (run on every merge, about 20 s):
`aw-arm-alu aw-thumb-alu memory timer-reload dma-priority tonc-snd1`

### Phase 0 - skeleton and contracts (1 agent) [MUST-HAVE]
- Owns: everything in section 2.
- Gate: wasm builds, subset grade runs with no trap, `cargo test` has at least one bus round-trip test.

### Phase 1 - CPU and "just enough" display (4 agents) [MUST-HAVE]
| Agent | Owns | Dev test |
|---|---|---|
| CPU core | `cpu/mod.rs`, `cpu/alu.rs` | unit tests: flags, shifter edge cases (shift by 0/32/>32), mode banking |
| ARM | `cpu/arm.rs` | `jsmolka/arm.gba` via `run_rom` (it shows a failing test number), armwrestler ARM pages |
| THUMB | `cpu/thumb.rs` | `jsmolka/thumb.gba`, armwrestler THUMB pages |
| PPU basic | `ppu/mod.rs`, `ppu/bitmap.rs`, `ppu/bg_text.rs`, `keypad.rs` | `jsmolka/ppu-hello.gba`, `tonc/m3-demo.gba`; line timing, VCOUNT, VBlank IRQ |

The CPU core agent starts first and lands the register file, `alu.rs` and the condition codes in about
the first fifth of the phase. ARM and THUMB then build on those, and the PPU agent works independently
from the start. Test ROMs need a working display, which is why basic PPU belongs in this phase.

- Gate (graded): `aw-arm-alu aw-arm-ldr-str aw-arm-ldm-stm aw-thumb-alu aw-thumb-ldr-str aw-thumb-ldm-stm
  mgba-shifter mgba-carry mgba-multiply-long` mostly at 1.0.
- Full grade at the end of this phase. First recorded milestone.

### Phase 2 - interrupts, timers, DMA, memory details (3 agents) [MUST-HAVE]
| Agent | Owns | Graded tests |
|---|---|---|
| IRQ / halt | `irq.rs` (integrator hands over ownership), CPU exception entry, HALTCNT | `ppu-vram-mirror`; dev: `nba-hw/haltcnt.gba`, `nba-hw/irq-irq-delay.gba`, `destoer/if-ack.gba`, `tonc/irq-demo.gba` |
| Timers | `timer.rs` | `timer-reload timer-start-stop`; dev: `tonc/tmr-demo.gba` |
| DMA | `dma.rs` | `dma-priority mgba-dma`; dev: `nba-hw/dma-*.gba`, `tonc/dma-demo.gba` |

The integrator handles memory and bus details in `bus.rs`: wait states, mirroring, open bus,
misaligned access. Gate tests: `memory mgba-io-read`.

- Gate: all 16 procedural tests graded, procedural section above 0.6 (ceiling 0.8).
- Full grade at the end of this phase.

### Phase 3 - full graphics (3 agents) [MUST-HAVE]
| Agent | Owns | Dev tests |
|---|---|---|
| Sprites | `ppu/obj.rs` | `tonc/obj-demo.gba`, `tonc/obj-aff.gba`, `nba-hw/ppu-sprite-hmosaic.gba` |
| Affine + bitmap | `ppu/bg_affine.rs`, `ppu/bitmap.rs` | `tonc/sbb-aff.gba`, `tonc/m7-demo.gba`, `tonc/bm-modes.gba`, `tonc/pageflip.gba`, `nba-hw/ppu-bgx.gba` |
| Effects + compositor | `ppu/effects.rs`, compositor in `ppu/mod.rs` | `tonc/win-demo.gba`, `tonc/bld-demo.gba`, `tonc/mos-demo.gba`, `tonc/prio-demo.gba`, `destoer/window-midframe.gba` |

Contract for this phase: each layer renders one scanline into a `[LayerPixel; 240]` holding colour,
priority, "is transparent" and "is semi-transparent sprite". Only the compositor merges layers.

- Gate (graded, replay subset): `spout-gameplay piugba-gameplay tonc-snd1` video scores up from Phase 2.
- Full grade at the end of this phase. The replay section should now be clearly above the baseline's 0.596.

### Phase 4 - sound (2 agents) [STRETCH]
| Agent | Owns | Graded tests |
|---|---|---|
| PSG | `apu/psg.rs` | `tonc-snd1 chip-advance-gameplay` (audio score) |
| FIFO + mixer | `apu/fifo.rs`, `apu/mod.rs` | `celeste-gameplay piugba-gameplay` (audio score); dev: `misc/gba-sound-demo-rates.gba` |

Critical: the grader analyses your audio at **Mesen2's sample rate**, which is
`32768 << SOUNDBIAS resolution bits` (32/65/131/262 kHz depending on what the game writes). Your
`emu_audio_rate()` and the number of samples per frame must follow the same rule, or the spectrum
will be wrong even if the sound is right.

- Gate: audio section above the baseline's 0.399.

### Phase 5 - game compatibility and timing (2-3 agents, one per failing game) [STRETCH]
- Cartridge saves (SRAM / Flash / EEPROM detection) and GPIO (`collie-defense` uses rumble) in `cart.rs`.
- Cycle accuracy: instruction timings (gbatek "ARM CPU Instruction Cycle Times"), wait states,
  prefetch. This is what keeps replays in sync with Mesen2.
- Method: pick the game with the lowest replay score, open its `.cand.png` and `.ref.png`, and find the
  first frame where they differ (`--emit-video` on the grader, or the `dump` tool in `$GBA_EVAL/harness`).
- Gate: every replay above 0.5, overall above 0.534.

### Phase 6 - performance and hardening (1 agent) [STRETCH]
- The fuel limit is 500M wasm instructions per frame. Measure the slowest replay and leave at least
  2x headroom.
- Determinism: `emu_reset()` must produce exactly the same state as `emu_load_rom()`.
  Add a test: run 100 frames, reset, run 100 frames, and compare the framebuffer hashes.

---

## 4. Workflow: agents, review, tracking

**Parallel agents.**
- Agent definitions live in `.claude/agents/`, one per role below plus `reviewer`. Prompts per phase
  are in `EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md`.
- Give each agent its own git worktree and branch (`phase1/arm`, `phase1/thumb`, ...).
- An agent only edits the files it owns in the phase table. Shared files belong to the integrator
  (you, or one coordinating agent).
- Brief each agent with three things: its phase row, `CLAUDE.md`, and its gbatek sections.
- Keep it to 4 agents at most per phase. More than that and integration costs more than it saves.

**Fast feedback loop (minutes, not 10).**
- Unit tests (`cargo test`, native, seconds) for decoder and ALU edge cases.
- `cargo run --bin run_rom -- <rom> <frames> out.ppm` for any ROM, including the ungraded dev ROMs
  under `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/test/`. Many of them print PASS/FAIL or a failing test number on screen.
- `scripts/grade-subset.sh <wasm> <run-name> <testcase ids...>` grades only the named testcases with
  the real grader (2 short tests took about 7 s). Read the per-testcase lines it prints. The section
  totals are meaningless for a subset.

**Milestone loop (about 10 min).** Run `scripts/grade-full.sh phase-<n> "note"` at the end of each phase,
after committing. It builds the wasm, runs the full grader, appends a row to `scores.tsv`
(date, phase, commit, overall, replay, procedural, audio, note), and saves `summary.json` plus the score row
under `results/milestones/phase-<n>/`. Commit both. All other `results/` output is git-ignored.

**Merge checklist (integrator).**
1. The branch only touches the files it owns.
2. `cargo test` and the wasm build pass.
3. The smoke set does not regress. The phase gate tests improve.
4. A review agent, which did not write the code, reads the diff against the gbatek sections. It checks
   for mistakes and for anything that looks like it came from another emulator (unusual names, comments
   or structure that the spec doesn't explain). Use a fresh context with no access to the author's chat.
5. Merge to `main`, then rerun the smoke set on `main`.

**Tracking.**
- `scores.tsv` holds one row per milestone, and `results/milestones/` holds each milestone's `summary.json`.
- `NOTES.md` logs decisions (date, what, why) and the agents and models used per phase.
- `TIMELOG.md` is the human's own hours log.
- Keep the `results/` folders of the last good run per phase, so you can diff `.cand.png` files when
  something regresses.

---

## 5. Risks and likely problems

1. **CPU bugs look like graphics bugs.** A wrong flag in one instruction can show up as a broken sprite
   three phases later. Finish Phase 1 properly, using the ungraded jsmolka ROMs, before moving on.
2. **Replay drift.** Small timing errors shift the moment input lands, and the game diverges. This is
   the biggest score risk and the hardest to debug. Mitigate by checking frame alignment in Phase 0 and
   doing cycle timing in Phase 5.
3. **Frame boundary mismatch.** If `emu_run_frame` stops at a different point in the frame than Mesen2,
   every frame is offset. Check this against the reference early.
4. **Audio rate mismatch.** See Phase 4. Easy to get silently wrong.
5. **Games hanging on save hardware.** Many games wait forever for a Flash or EEPROM reply. A black
   screen on a replay usually means this.
6. **Shared-file conflicts** between parallel agents. Prevented by the ownership table. Expect
   contract changes anyway and route them through the integrator.
7. **Originality.**
   - Models have seen open-source emulators in training and may reproduce their structure.
   - The review step checks for this, and `.claude/settings.json` blocks reads of
     `gba-eval/candidates`, `gba-eval/third_party`, `mesen_step.cpp` and web access.
   - The block only applies to Claude Code agents launched from this repo. Other agent tools need
     the same rule in their own config.
   - Shell commands that don't name those folders directly can still reach them. Treat the block as a
     guard rail, not proof.
8. **Overfitting.** An agent may "fix" a test by special-casing it. `CLAUDE.md` forbids branching on ROM
   identity, and the review step checks for it.
9. **Endstate tests are all-or-nothing.** One wrong pixel scores ~0. A test that "looks right" can
   still score 0. Compare `.cand.png` with `.ref.png` pixel by pixel.
10. **Fuel limit.** A slow PPU (per-pixel work with lots of branching) can trap on heavy games.
    Measure in Phase 6, or earlier if a replay "skips".
11. **Score ceiling.** The maximum is 0.96, not 1.0 (the `comprehensive` subsystem has no tests). Tell the
    client so expectations are set correctly.
12. **Grader runtime.** A full grade takes about 10 minutes and uses all CPU cores. Running two at once
    slows both. Set `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` if you must.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fast feedback: grade a wasm against only the testcases you name.
#
#   scripts/grade-subset.sh <wasm> <run-name> <testcase-id>...
#   scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm cpu aw-arm-alu mgba-carry
#
# Builds a throwaway corpus (filtered testcases.json + the real ROMs,
# replays and reference cache mounted read-only) and runs the same
# gba-eval-grader docker image as the full grade. Results land in
# results/<run-name>/ in this repo. Section scores in summary.json are
# meaningless for a subset (missing subsystems count as 0); read the
# per-testcase entries instead.
set -euo pipefail

GBA_EVAL="${GBA_EVAL:-/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval}"
[ $# -ge 3 ] || { sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 2; }
WASM="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd)/$(basename "$1")"; NAME="$2"; shift 2
[ -f "$WASM" ] || { echo "error: $WASM not found" >&2; exit 1; }

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
OUT="$ROOT/results/$NAME"; SUBSET="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$SUBSET"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$OUT"

python3 -I - "$GBA_EVAL/corpus/testcases.json" "$SUBSET/testcases.json" "$@" <<'PY'
import json, sys
src, dst, *ids = sys.argv[1:]
data = json.load(open(src))
cases = data if isinstance(data, list) else data["testcases"]
picked = [c for c in cases if c["id"] in ids]
missing = set(ids) - {c["id"] for c in picked}
if missing:
    sys.exit(f"unknown testcase id(s): {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
json.dump(picked if isinstance(data, list) else {**data, "testcases": picked}, open(dst, "w"), indent=1)
PY
cp "$GBA_EVAL/corpus/grader.yaml" "$SUBSET/"

docker run --rm \
    -v "$GBA_EVAL":/repo:ro \
    -v "$SUBSET":/subset \
    -v "$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms":/subset/roms:ro \
    -v "$GBA_EVAL/corpus/replays":/subset/replays:ro \
    -v "$GBA_EVAL/corpus/reference-cache":/subset/reference-cache:ro \
    -v "$(dirname "$WASM")":/wasm:ro \
    -v "$OUT":/out \
    gba-eval-grader /wasm/"$(basename "$WASM")" /subset/ /out

python3 -I - "$OUT" <<'PY'
import json, sys
s = json.load(open(f"{sys.argv[1]}/summary.json"))
for tc, r in sorted(s["per_testcase"].items()):
    print(f"{tc:28} video={r.get('video_score')!s:22} audio={r.get('audio_score')}")
PY

## Decisions

| Date | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-05 | Single Rust crate `gba_emu` (`cdylib` + `rlib`), one module per subsystem | One file per owner keeps parallel agents from editing the same file; `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native debug binary run without wasm. |
| 2026-11-05 | Phase 0 fixes all shared contracts (bus, IO dispatch, IRQ, cycle timing, ABI) before any parallel work | Parallel agents otherwise invent incompatible interfaces and merges conflict. |
| 2026-11-05 | Fast loop = `cargo test` + `run_rom` + `scripts/grade-subset.sh`; full grade (~10 min) only at milestones | A full grade measured ~10 min; 2-test subset measured ~7 s. |
| 2026-11-05 | Phases 0-3 must-have, 4-6 stretch | Time-limited; a verified 0-3 beats a broken 0-6. Graphics carry 60% of the score through replays. |
| 2026-11-05 | No reading of `gba-eval/candidates`, Mesen2 source or other emulators; enforced by CLAUDE.md, `.claude/settings.json` deny rules and the reviewer agent | Client requires original code. Deny rules are a guard rail only; the reviewer is the real check. |
| 2026-11-05 | Audio must be produced at Mesen2's rate (`32768 << SOUNDBIAS resolution`) | The grader analyses candidate audio at the reference's rate (`lockstep/src/lib.rs`), so a different rate distorts the spectrum. |
| 2026-11-05 | Score ceiling noted as 0.96 | `comprehensive` has weight 0.20 in procedural but no testcases, so it always scores 0. |
| 2026-11-05 | Baseline to beat: 0.5345 overall (replay 0.596, procedural 0.486, audio 0.399) | Full grade of `candidates/gba-core/gba_core_shim.wasm`, run as a binary only; its source was not read. |
| 2026-11-05 | Worker branches merged with `--no-ff` after a fresh-context reviewer; max 2 review/fix rounds, then escalate to the human | Keeps each worker's changes traceable and stops agents looping on the same failure. |
| 2026-11-05 | Each milestone is tagged `phase-<N>` and committed with `results/milestones/phase-<N>/`; agents never push, the human pushes | Gives a known-good point to roll back to; the human controls what reaches GitHub. |
| 2026-11-05 | Added "Code readability" rules to CLAUDE.md (descriptive names, commented gbatek register names, doc comment naming the gbatek section, small functions); reviewer checks them | Client and human must be able to read and verify the code; the gbatek references make review against the spec fast. |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Display status and Interrupt control. The H-Blank conditions are generated once
per scanline, including for the 'hidden' scanlines during V-Blank.

  Bit   Expl.
  0     V-Blank flag   (Read only) (1=VBlank) (set in line 160..226; not 227)
  1     H-Blank flag   (Read only) (1=HBlank) (toggled in all lines, 0..227)
  2     V-Counter flag (Read only) (1=Match)  (set in selected line)     (R)
  3     V-Blank IRQ Enable         (1=Enable)                          (R/W)
  4     H-Blank IRQ Enable         (1=Enable)                          (R/W)
  5     V-Counter IRQ Enable       (1=Enable)                          (R/W)
  6     Not used (0) / DSi: LCD Initialization Ready (0=Busy, 1=Ready)   (R)
  7     Not used (0) / NDS: MSB of V-Vcount Setting (LYC.Bit8) (0..262)(R/W)
  8-15  V-Count Setting (LYC)      (0..227)                            (R/W)

The V-Count-Setting value is much the same as LYC of older gameboys, when its
value is identical to the content of the VCOUNT register then the V-Counter
flag is set (Bit 2), and (if enabled in Bit 5) an interrupt is requested.
Although the drawing time is only 960 cycles (240*4), the H-Blank flag is "0"
for a total of 1006 cycles.

  8     Not used (0) / NDS: MSB of Current Scanline (LY.Bit8) (0..262)   (R)
  9-15  Not Used (0)

Note: This is much the same than the 'LY' register of older gameboys.

The Phase 0 skeleton is built and committed on branch `phase0/skeleton` (5 commits, not pushed). The wasm builds with no import section, `cargo test` passes (6 tests), `run_rom` writes a .ppm, and the subset grade runs all 6 tests with no "trapped" skip. One thing needs your decision: I changed the owner write signature to `io_write16(offset, value, mask)` instead of the plan's `io_write16(offset, value)` (item 3a).

## 1. What I built and the commits

Worktree: `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac23e34c0c2f986ed`

- **Bus** (`src/bus.rs`): reads and writes at 8, 16 and 32 bits for every region, including the EWRAM, IWRAM and VRAM mirrors. Each access adds a cost to `bus.access_cycles` (default wait states from the gbatek table), and the CPU collects it with `take_access_cycles()`. The BIOS comes from `assets/gba_bios_stub.bin` via `include_bytes!` at 0x0. Byte writes to palette and VRAM go into both halves; OAM ignores them.
- **IO** (`src/io.rs`): dispatch table with the exact owner ranges from the plan. 8- and 32-bit accesses are split here. It also has a shared `merge()` helper, a `PlainRegisters<N>` storage type, and the serial stub.
- **IRQ** (`src/irq.rs`): `IrqSource`, `request()`, `pending()`. IE, IF (writing 1 clears a bit) and IME work, HALTCNT sets `halt_requested`, and the rest of 0x200-0x804 is plain storage.
- **PPU** (`src/ppu/mod.rs`): line timing works now: VCOUNT, the DISPSTAT VBlank (lines 160-226), HBlank and VCount-match flags, and their three IRQs. It returns `PpuEvents { hblank_started, vblank_started }` for DMA. Every line is drawn black. The `LayerPixel` type for Phase 3 is defined here, with transparent-filling stubs for each layer.
- **Other components**: storing stubs for the CPU (reset state, burns 1 cycle per step), timers, DMA (`dma::run_pending_transfers(&mut Bus)`), keypad and cart. The APU produces silence at `32768 << SOUNDBIAS resolution` Hz.
- **Frame loop** (`src/gba.rs`): `Gba` owns `Cpu` and `Bus`, and the bus owns every other component. That ownership choice keeps Rust borrowing simple. `run_frame()` runs exactly 280,896 cycles per frame and passes events between components with plain method calls. The frame-end point is the constant `FRAME_END_LINE` (currently 160).
- **ABI** (`src/lib.rs`): the 10 exports. The ROM buffer, framebuffer and audio buffer live outside `Gba`, so their pointers stay valid across load and reset. `emu_boot_frames` is not exported.
- **`src/bin/run_rom.rs`**: `run_rom <rom> <frames> out.ppm [out.wav]`. It goes through the ABI functions.

Commits:
- `c35ffeb` chore(abi): add crate manifest, wasm build alias and BIOS stub asset
- `8a539d3` feat(bus): add memory map, IO dispatch table and interrupt controller
- `a7c51c3` feat(ppu): add component stubs with PPU line timing
- `7b2f568` feat(abi): add frame loop and the 10 ABI exports

## 3. Unfinished work, guesses and contract changes

**a. Contract change: writes carry a byte mask.** Every owner implements `io_write16(offset, value, mask)`, where `mask` is 0x00FF, 0xFF00 or 0xFFFF. Reads stay `io_read16(offset)`. I added the mask because splitting an 8-bit write into a read-modify-write of 16 bits gives wrong results in some cases:
- A byte write that acknowledges IF would clear the other byte's pending bits.
- A byte write to POSTFLG would also re-trigger HALTCNT.
- Sound FIFO bytes and write-only registers would be corrupted.

The BIOS stub's halt is itself a byte write (`strb` to 0x4000301). Owners apply the mask with `io::merge`, and there is a test for the IF case. If you want the plan's exact 2-argument form instead, the alternative is that io.rs keeps a copy of the last-written values to merge against, plus exceptions for IF and HALTCNT.

**b. Frame boundary not checked against Mesen2.** That can't be done with a stub CPU. `FRAME_END_LINE = 160`, so the first frame after reset is 197,120 cycles and every later one is 280,896. Setting it to 0 makes every frame full length.

**c. HBlank start is a guess.** I used cycle 1006, from the DISPSTAT note that the flag stays 0 for 1006 cycles, rather than 960. The HBlank IRQ and HBlank DMA fire at the same point. It's one constant, `HBLANK_START_CYCLE`.

**d. gbatek contradicts itself on HBlank IRQs during VBlank.** The LCD Timings section says there are none; the DISPSTAT section says they happen on every line. I followed DISPSTAT (IRQ on every line), with HBlank DMA only on visible lines.

**e. Known shortcuts, each marked `ponytail:` in the code:**
- No WAITCNT and no sequential/non-sequential cycle split.
- Unmapped addresses and reads past the end of the ROM return 0 instead of open-bus values; no BIOS read protection.
- Misaligned addresses are rounded down to alignment.
- VRAM byte writes into the sprite area are not ignored.
- KEYCNT is stored but the keypad IRQ is not raised.
- HALTCNT "stop" mode is treated as halt.

**f. CPU halt is not wired up.** The stub CPU ignores `halt_requested`; that belongs to the CPU and IRQ agents.

## 4. Decisions for NOTES.md (2026-11-05)

- **IO writes take a byte mask** (`io_write16(offset, value, mask)`, 8/32-bit split in io.rs). Why: a read-modify-write split breaks IF acknowledge, HALTCNT vs POSTFLG, the FIFOs and write-only registers.
- **`Bus` owns every component except the CPU, and the PPU owns palette, VRAM and OAM.** Why: the CPU only sees the bus, and gba.rs can borrow sibling fields (`bus.ppu.step(c, &mut bus.irq)`) without reference cycles. DMA transfers are a free function taking `&mut Bus`.
- **Frame end is `gba::FRAME_END_LINE` (160), with leftover cycles carried into the next frame.** Why: exact 280,896-cycle frames, and the boundary can be tuned in one place against Mesen2.
- **The framebuffer, audio buffer and ROM buffer are kept outside `Gba`, and the framebuffer is copied after each frame.** Why: ABI pointers stay stable across load and reset; the copy costs about 38K writes per frame.
- **Bus access costs add up in `bus.access_cycles`, and the CPU drains them with `take_access_cycles()`.** Why: the read/write signatures stay `read32(addr) -> u32` as the plan specifies.
- **The APU stub emits silent samples at `32768 << SOUNDBIAS[15:14]` Hz.** Why: the host gets the right number of samples per frame from day one.
- **`cargo wasm` alias added in `.cargo/config.toml`, and the dev profile uses opt-level 2.** Why: a quicker wasm build command, and ROMs run in tests at usable speed.
